title: Equivariant smooth Galois alteration model before imposing degree conditions
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $B$ be a nonempty normal proper finite-type $e$-scheme which is a finite disjoint union of integral schemes and is geometrically reduced over $e$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $C_B\subseteq B$ be the support of an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. There are a finite extension $K/e$ [def-pc-field-extension], a finite group $G$ acting on $K$ by $e$-automorphisms, a smooth projective $K$-scheme $Y$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-kun-projective], and a projective surjective morphism $h:Y\to B$ [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The group $G$ acts on $Y$ by $e$-scheme automorphisms, $h$ is invariant, and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is equivariant. The extension $K^G/e$ is purely inseparable. The morphism $h$ sends every generic point of $Y$ to a generic point of $B$, with finite residue-field extension [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-generic-point] [def-weil-residue-field]. The finite scheme quotient $q_G:Y\to Y/G$ exists and there is a dense open $U\subseteq B$, meeting every component, such that $(Y/G)\times_B U\to U$ is a finite universal homeomorphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. The quotient has orbit geometric fibres, has invariant structure sheaf, and is categorical for invariant morphisms. The reduced inverse image $(h^{-1}C_B)_{\rm red}$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor on $Y/K$ [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. This means that it is a reduced effective Cartier divisor with finitely many distinct integral components, and every intersection of $r$ distinct components is empty or smooth over $K$ of pure codimension $r$, including $r=0$, when the intersection is $Y$. All quotients by subgroups of $G$ also exist and are finite quotients with these orbit and invariant-sheaf properties. Projective over a field means a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space. No degree condition is imposed on $K/e$ or $h$. The empty divisor is allowed. Field-extension terminology and degrees are as in [def-pc-field-tower].

The common constants and group are obtained simultaneously before choosing any Sylow subgroup; for disconnected B use all its finitely many components, not separate prime-degree constant fields.

proof.text: Write $B=\coprod_jB_j$ as given. For each $B_j$ apply the Galois component presentation, obtaining $e_{0j},X_j,H_j,u_j$. Let $Z_j$ be the support of the invariant Cartier pullback $u_j^*C_B$. It is nowhere dense: a Cartier equation is nonzero in the integral local domains, hence is nonzero at the generic point.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, p.150, geometric components and decomposition groups.

proof.text: Apply the marked plurinodal alteration to $(X_j/e_{0j},H_j,Z_j)$, obtaining $F_j,J_j,\rho_j:J_j\twoheadrightarrow H_j$, tower $(T_{ji},Z_{ji})$ and alteration $a_j$. Resolve this quasi-split marked tower by the tower-resolution node. Write $r_j:S_j\to T_{jd_j}$ for its top modification. It is birational, $S_j/F_j$ is integral smooth projective, and $D_j=((u_ja_jr_j)^{-1}C_B)_{\rm red}$ is relative SNC, since $a_j^{-1}Z_j\subseteq Z_{jd_j}$.

source.place: X Lemma 2.2 proof, pp.149--150; returned Steps 2--4.

proof.text: Put $v_j=u_ja_jr_j$. Its geometric generic fibre is a single $J_j$-orbit: the images in $X_j$ form one $H_j$-orbit; lift an element of $H_j$ along $\rho_j$ to match two images, then use $\ker\rho_j$ to match the points. Birational $r_j$ leaves the generic fields and these generic fibres unchanged. Thus $v_j$ is invariant and surjective and sends its generic point to that of $B_j$ with finite residue extension.

source.place: X 2.2(iii) and X 2.3 Step 2; returned Step 5.

proof.text: Apply common-field semilinear induction to $(F_j,J_j,S_j,v_j)$. It supplies $K,G,\Gamma_j,Y_j$ and $Y=\coprod_jY_j$ with invariant $h:Y\to B$, purely inseparable $K^G/e$, and the required generic-point and geometric generic orbit assertions. Apply geometric permanence for this induced family: $Y/K$ is smooth projective, $Y/e$ is projective, $h$ is projective surjective, and $(h^{-1}C_B)_{\rm red}$ is relative SNC.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, diagram (2.b), pp.150--151; returned Steps 6--7.

proof.text: Apply the generic-orbit quotient node to this $Y,G,h,B$. Its hypotheses, including reducedness of $Y$, hold by the preceding steps. It gives all subgroup quotients, with orbit geometric fibres, invariant structure sheaves and categorical factorization, and a dense open meeting every component over which $Y/G\to B$ is finite and a universal homeomorphism. Together with the preceding $K,G,Y,h$ and boundary this is every assertion of the item.

lean.statement: theorem exists_equivariant_smooth_galois_model (e : Type u) [Field e] (B : Scheme.{u}) (b : B ⟶ Spec (.of e)) [Nonempty B] [IsProper b] [GeometricallyReduced b] (hBnormal : ∀ x : B, IsDomain (B.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (B.presheaf.stalk x)) (hBcomponents : ∃ (n : ℕ) (V : Fin n → B.Opens), (∀ i, IsIntegral (V i).toScheme) ∧ Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (V i) (V j)) ∧ (⨆ i, V i) = ⊤) (C : B.IdealSheafData) (hC : C.IsInvertible) : ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (_ : Algebra e K), Module.Finite e K ∧ ∃ (G : Type u) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G) (ρ : G →* (K ≃ₐ[e] K)), IsPurelyInseparable e (IntermediateField.fixedField ρ.range) ∧ ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (p : Y ⟶ Spec (.of K)) (a : G →* Aut Y) (h : Y ⟶ B), Smooth p ∧ IsHProjective p ∧ IsProjectiveBundle h ∧ Surjective h ∧ h ≫ b = p ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap e K)) ∧ (∀ g : G, (a g).hom ≫ h = h) ∧ (∀ g : G, (a g).hom ≫ p = p ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (ρ g⁻¹).toRingHom)) ∧ (∀ y ∈ genericPoints Y, h y ∈ genericPoints B ∧ (h.residueFieldMap y).hom.Finite) ∧ (C.comap h).radical.IsSmoothStrictNormalCrossingsDivisor p ∧ ∃ (Q : Subgroup G → Scheme.{u}) (q : ∀ H : Subgroup G, Y ⟶ Q H) (d : ∀ H : Subgroup G, Q H ⟶ B), (∀ H : Subgroup G, IsAdmissibleFiniteSchemeQuotient (a.comp H.subtype) (q H)) ∧ (∀ (H : Subgroup G) (T : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ T), (∀ g : H, (a g).hom ≫ f = f) → ∃! r : Q H ⟶ T, q H ≫ r = f) ∧ (∀ (H : Subgroup G) (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω], Function.Surjective (fun t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y ↦ t ≫ q H) ∧ ∀ t₁ t₂ : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y, t₁ ≫ q H = t₂ ≫ q H ↔ ∃ g : H, t₁ ≫ (a g).hom = t₂) ∧ (∀ H : Subgroup G, q H ≫ d H = h) ∧ ∃ U : B.Opens, Dense (U : Set B) ∧ (∀ x ∈ genericPoints B, x ∈ U) ∧ IsFinite ((d ⊤).resLE U ((d ⊤) ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl) ∧ (topologically IsHomeomorph).universally ((d ⊤).resLE U ((d ⊤) ⁻¹ᵁ U) le_rfl)
